chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far the First (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man comes to own his parents, or his sister, or his maternal aunt, or his paternal aunt, they are automatically emancipated. But he may own the son of his brother, and his paternal uncle; and he may own his brother, his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle through the breastfeeding relationship.

key_terms.الرَّضَاعَة: The breastfeeding/nursing relationship; creates legal kinship bonds similar to blood relations in many rulings
key_terms.عَتَقُوا: They are freed/emancipated (itq); automatic manumission without need for a formal act
key_terms.مَلَكَ: To own/possess as a slave; the causative context is coming into ownership of a person

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Baqir, what happens when a man comes to own his close relatives in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a fundamental ruling in Islamic law concerning the automatic manumission (itq) of close blood relatives if they come into a person's ownership through slavery. The ruling addresses the intersection of family ties and the institution of slavery: certain mahram relatives (parents, sister, maternal aunt, paternal aunt) are automatically freed upon ownership, while more distant relatives and milk-relations may be owned. This hadith reflects the Islamic legal principle that family dignity and blood ties take precedence over the right of ownership.
